answer: One defense is accountable vouching: a new identity joins only when three established peers endorse it publicly, each staking reputation on that endorsement. An attacker cannot forge supporters from nothing, because every fake needs real sponsors willing to risk their own standing. If the newcomer cheats, blame ripples back to its endorsers, who lose weight and face review. A trustworthy identity thus gains a pigment of endorsements from unrelated peers, while a Sybil cluster betrays itself: its endorsements loop only among its own members, a closed circle peers can spot and refuse.
